definitions.explanation: Behavior or a person that lacks proper manners or etiquette. Implies a violation of social norms or established codes of conduct.

examples.japanese: {無作法|ぶさほう}な⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦よくない→いい：00118_ii⟧。
examples.english: An ill-mannered attitude is not good.

examples.japanese: {食事中|しょくじちゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦スマホ→スマホ：04721_sumaho⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{無作法|ぶさほう}だ。
examples.english: Looking at your smartphone during a meal is bad manners.

examples.japanese: ⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦あくびをする→あくびをする：25803_akubiwosuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、なん⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{無作法|ぶさほう}な⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧だろう。
examples.english: To yawn in front of a guest — what an ill-mannered person.

notes:
USAGE:
Can function as both a na-adjective ({無作法|ぶさほう}な) and a noun ({無作法|ぶさほう}). The word carries a somewhat formal or old-fashioned tone. In everyday speech, ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧ (badly behaved) or ⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧ (rude) are more common alternatives.

WRITING:
{無|ぶ} (without) + ⟦{作法|さほう}→作法：02825_sahou⟧ (etiquette, manners). The reading ぶ for {無|ぶ} is the on'yomi prefix meaning "without" or "lacking."

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{作法|さほう}→作法：02825_sahou⟧: manners, etiquette
- ⟦{行儀|ぎょうぎ}→行儀：02662_gyougi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧: badly behaved, ill-mannered
- ⟦{失礼|しつれい}→失礼：01247_shitsurei⟧: rude, impolite

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無作法|ぶさほう}な⟦{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}い→振る舞い：10520_furumai⟧: ill-mannered behavior
- {無作法|ぶさほう}な⟦{態度|たいど}→態度：03396_taido⟧: rude attitude
- {無作法|ぶさほう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{詫|わ}びる→詫びる：14174_wabiru⟧: to apologize for one's rudeness
